newsitem.title: JAPAN: Minor Metals - Asia quiet except vanadium, gallium.
newsitem.headline: Minor Metals - Asia quiet except vanadium, gallium.

text.p: Asia's strategic metals markets have been quiet this week, but a few trades were heard done in gallium and vanadium, regional traders said on Tuesday.
Chinese 98 percent grade vanadium pentoxide was heard offered at $3.25 per pound, CIF Japan.
Chinese vanadium was said quoted at $15.30 per kg.
"We had some trades for Chinese vanadium this week," a trader at a major trade house in Tokyo said.
"But Japanese end-users have almost covered their near-term demand through long-term contracts, and are unlikely to buy actively in the spot market at the moment," he said.
Glencore International South Africa marketing director Les Ford said on Monday that prices were stable because there was less Chinese vanadium available on world markets.
Lower special steel production in Japan this year has helped trim domestic demand for vanadium and other rare metals, Tokyo traders said.

Japan's special steel output in the January-September period totalled 11,288,431 tonnes, down by 8.7 percent from the same period last year, according to Ministry of International Trade and Industry statistics.
Instead, overseas consumers were heard negotiating for about 300 to 500 kg of Chinese germanium for March/April shipment at roughly $800-$900 per kilo CIF the United States.
This compared to the current spot price of $1,000 per kg.
Cobalt was said to be bearish as China had adequate stocks, and the 99.3 percent grade was heard at $20.60/20.70 per pound, CIF Hong Kong from Europe.
The domestic Chinese price for the same grade was said to be around 420,000 yuan ($50,602) per tonne.
